name: Rhode Island

regulator.name: Rhode Island Department of State, Business Services

law.name: Uniform Athlete Agents Act (R.I. Gen. Laws 5-74.1)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. The act covers endorsement contracts.
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete: If you sign this contract: (1) You may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport; (2) If you have an athletic director, within seventy-two (72) hours after entering into this contract, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director; and (3) You may cancel this contract within fourteen (14) days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility.
summary: Register with the Department of State. $50.

steps.text: Fill out Form 661, Registration of Athlete Agent

steps.detail: Check to RI Department of State.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Only reach out first to athletes who have finished college eligibility
steps.detail: If an athlete still has eligibility, wait for them to contact you. Then tell the athletic director before you reply. For a minor, contact the parents.

steps.text: Give the athletic director any info before you give it to the athlete
Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, other pay you get for the deal, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to student athlete in bold capital letters next to their signature
Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete must tell them too. The athlete may cancel within 14 days.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Rhode Island and federal law (SPARTA) ban predating or postdating it.
Each client's name and address, each contract and what you spent to recruit each athlete. The Secretary of State may inspect them.

steps.text: Never give an athlete anything of value before they sign, or make false promises
steps.detail: Don't pay anyone else to steer them to you either, unless it's another registered agent.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: Not re-read on 2026-10-28: whether endorsement deals are covered (5-74.1-2). The $50 and $25 fees (5-74.1-9) and the 2-year term (5-74.1-6) were confirmed the same day.
No Rhode Island NIL law changing agent rules was checked. Search the 2021 to 2026 Rhode Island session laws for NIL bills.
